note: Files (all in git, read from the checkout; fetched with git show HEAD into runs/theory-tests/r7-m09/ if missing): day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, wsp1/full500/sft1_plain-01/per_problem.json. E4 = problems with exactly 4 attempt-0 base rows, all score_v3 == 1 and cap_hit not true. First row per problem_index in each per_problem.json (each has 500 rows, one per problem, so this is a no-op). W = cue score_v3 == 0 and not cap hit. Plain wrong = score_v3 == 0 or cap_hit true; problems with a missing plain row or null non-cap score are dropped (none seen in the format check: score_v3 is always an int). Bootstrap over kept W problems, entries (cue row, plain row); n = kept W size. alt_measured: recurrence counted only as a finished v3-wrong plain answer (plain cap hits not counted), since the mechanism is a deterministic format miss. Caveats: W is likely small (tens of problems), so the interval is wide; Think-SFT texts are not stored, so a plain-wrong can be a real error as well as a format miss.

Same files and E4/W as k=1. Gold = gold field of the first attempt-0 base row in file order. Normalisation exactly as written: strip, drop '$', drop all whitespace, unwrap a whole \boxed{...} (brace-matched so that '\boxed{a}+\boxed{b}' is not unwrapped), drop thousands commas with the given regex, integer iff ^-?\d+$. Bootstrap over W problems; n = |W|. alt_measured: integers carrying unit/decoration markup (^\circ, \%, \text{...}/\mbox{...}/\mathrm{...}, \! or \, spacing, leading +) also count as integers, since the recipe's 'plain integer' could mean integer value. Under the main reading golds like '90^\circ' or '10\%' or '\text{(C)}'-style letters count as non-integer, which can push the share up.

Files: day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl and wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json. E4 as in k=1. Wrong = score_v3 == 0 or cap_hit true; null non-cap rows excluded (none expected). Statistic = rows with cap_hit true / wrong rows, bootstrap over the wrong rows (one per problem); n = number of wrong rows. alt_measured: a row also counts as a cap hit (and wrong) if n_generated >= 16,384 even without the flag. Caveat: the denominator mixes W (finished wrong) and cap hits, so its size is |W| + cap hits.

Files: day1_3/math500_base_cue-01/rows.jsonl, wsp1/full500/sft1_cue-01/per_problem.json, rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json (T2 = RL plain, one sample). E4 as in k=1. Kept = E4 problems with a cue row not cap hit with non-null score_v3 and an RL row with non-null t2_generated_tokens. x = ln(max(n_generated,1)/max(t2_generated_tokens,1)); FW = score_v3 0, FR = score_v3 1; median of even count = mean of the two middle values. Prints a groups line {FW, FR}; n = min(|FW|, |FR|) (FW expected small). Bootstrap resamples the kept problems jointly; a resample with an empty FW or FR (rare) takes the full-sample value. FW < 3 -> refuted without number; FR empty -> not computable. alt_measured: same but also drops problems where RL (t2) hit the cap, since a capped RL length is a censored reference. Caveat: the RL reference is a single sample, so x is noisy per problem; n_generated and t2_generated_tokens come from different tokenizations/runs but the same Olmo-3 tokenizer family is assumed.
